text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A systematic review and meta-analysis reports that creatine supplementation enhanced memory performance in healthy individuals.","cited_pids":["60e469276e13#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The memory benefit of creatine is described as especially evident in older adults aged 66-76 years.","cited_pids":["60e469276e13#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A narrative review of creatine monohydrate in older adults lists memory among observed cognitive benefits.","cited_pids":["51a9f6b43450#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"The narrative review notes that creatine's cognitive benefits are primarily seen when combined with exercise training.","cited_pids":["51a9f6b43450#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A six-week trial in healthy young adults found creatine at moderate or high doses had no significant effect on cognitive performance.","cited_pids":["3d02a7e7575a#1"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"The six-week trial studied young adults rather than older adults.","cited_pids":["3d02a7e7575a#1"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A review on cognition and memory in older adults describes the potential and challenges of creatine.","cited_pids":["47c94ec99e80#0"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"The evidence for a memory benefit of creatine in older adults rests on a limited number of trials and reviews.","cited_pids":[]}]}
